memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord also said to Moses, "I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of the first male offspring of every Israelite woman. The Levites are mine, for all the firstborn are mine. When I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I set apart for myself every firstborn in Israel, whether human or animal. They are to be mine. I am the Lord." - Num 3:11-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God explains something remarkable here. The Levites were to be taken in place of the firstborn of Israel. On the night of the Passover in Egypt, God had spared Israel's firstborn while judgment fell on Egypt. Because of that, the firstborn belonged to Him in a special way. Now the Levites would stand in their place, given to God's service instead.

At the heart of this is the idea of substitution — one taken in the place of another. The whole tribe of Levi represented and stood in for the firstborn of the nation.

This principle runs like a golden thread through the whole Bible, and it points us straight to the gospel. On the cross, Jesus stood in our place. He took the judgment we deserved so that we could be spared. Just as the Levites were substituted for the firstborn, Christ was substituted for us — the innocent for the guilty, the one for the many (1 Pet 3:18).

"The Levites are mine," God says. And through Christ, He says the same over you: you are mine, purchased and set apart.

Rest today in the wonder of substitution. Someone was taken in your place. Because Jesus stood where you deserved to stand, you now belong to God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What does it mean to you that Christ took your place?
- How does belonging to God change how you live?
- Have you thanked God today for His saving substitution?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You for standing in my place and taking what I deserved. I am Yours — help me to live in the joy of belonging to You. Amen.
